steps.message: Two builds, two configurations, so I need two distinct binlogs rather than one build's log getting overwritten by the other. Using /bl:{} for both invocations lets MSBuild pick a unique filename each time instead of me hardcoding names that could collide.

results.content: Ran: dotnet build SimpleApp.csproj -c Debug "/bl:{}" -> Build succeeded, wrote a new *.binlog file.
Ran: dotnet build SimpleApp.csproj -c Release "/bl:{}" -> Build succeeded, wrote a second, differently-named *.binlog file.

steps.message: Both configurations built successfully and each has its own binlog since I used /bl:{} on both invocations (Debug and Release) -- the {} placeholder gave each run a unique name, so neither overwrote the other's log. If I'd used a fixed name like /bl:build.binlog for both, the Release binlog would have clobbered the Debug one.
